Wyoming Teams With Trump Administration to Expedite Energy, Industrial Projects

en.title: Amber Infrastructure Plans 10-15 Year Exits; Wyoming Teams with Trump Administration
en.dek: Amber Infrastructure plans 10‑15 year exits for Ukraine funds; Wyoming signs memo with Trump administration to speed permitting for large energy projects.
facts: Amber Infrastructure runs two Ukraine funds totaling €467 million, raised from international financial institutions and European public money.

body: Amber Infrastructure runs two Ukraine funds totaling €467 million, raised from international financial institutions and European public money. The funds target wind, distributed energy, and logistics, and are designed for exits over 10 to 15 years, according to Managing Director Dominykas Tuckus. The first close of Amber Dragon Ukraine Infrastructure Fund I was €207 million on May 27, with backing from the EBRD (€60 million), the EIB (€50 million), and the IFC (€40 million). The fund’s target size is €350 million, as stated by the EBRD.

Wyoming will partner with the Trump administration to streamline permitting for large energy and industrial projects. The initiative aims to expedite projects such as data centers, according to a press conference held on Monday. Gov. Mark Gordon and Federal Permitting Improvement Steering Council Executive Director Emily Domenech signed a memorandum during the event. The memorandum was announced by representatives from both groups, as reported by InsideClimate News.

Amber Infrastructure is among foreign investors that are not waiting for the war to end, according to Dominykas Tuckus, and the company is willing to risk investing in Ukraine while the war continues, as stated in the interview.
en.context: Ukraine has been seeking foreign investment to rebuild infrastructure amid ongoing conflict. Wyoming is partnering with the Trump administration to accelerate permitting for large energy and industrial projects.
